sources.title: Fluorinated gas F gas guidance for users producers and traders
facts: Environment Agency and Defra collection covers F-gas lists, quota, reporting, servicing, leak checks, recovery, labelling and bans.
Regulatory duties and equipment status do not by themselves establish atmospheric release or parcel emissions.

sources.title: Applying for quota to produce or import F gas
facts: GB HFC quota controls quantities placed on the market and is expressed in tonnes CO2 equivalent.
Quota allocation or use is not the same as physical F-gas release to atmosphere.

sources.title: Fluorinated greenhouse gases and ozone-depleting substances charging scheme
facts: Environment Agency charging scheme covers regulatory F-gas and ODS activities and updated charges.
A fee or charge is administrative evidence, not a physical greenhouse-gas quantity.

sources.title: Record and report F gas and equipment pre-charged with F gas
facts: Reporting thresholds cover production, import, export, destruction, feedstock and pre-charged equipment, with independent verification required for specified activities.
Reported market activity or a verification document must not be interpreted automatically as emitted mass.

sources.title: Fluorinated gases F gases list and global warming potentials
facts: Official guidance lists HFCs, PFCs, SF6 and other reportable gases with global warming potentials.
A gas GWP is a conversion property and does not establish how much gas was released.

sources.title: Calculate the carbon dioxide equivalent quantity of an F gas
facts: CO2 equivalent is calculated from F-gas mass multiplied by its GWP.
Contained, imported or quota F-gas mass converted to CO2e is not atmospheric emissions unless release/activity evidence supports that interpretation.

sources.title: Checking F gas equipment for leaks
facts: Leak-check frequency depends on CO2-equivalent charge and equipment conditions, and automatic leak detection changes intervals.
A leak-check obligation or equipment charge does not prove a leak occurred or quantify released mass.

sources.title: Record F gas in equipment you own or service
facts: Operators keep records of gas quantity, added gas, leak checks, recovery and disposal for qualifying equipment.
Equipment inventory and maintenance additions require explicit release evidence before being treated as emissions.

sources.title: Recovering reclaiming and recycling F gas
facts: Qualified technicians must recover F gas from specified equipment and recovered gas can be reclaimed, recycled or destroyed.
Recovered or recycled mass is not equivalent to atmospheric release and should not be double counted as emissions.

sources.title: Qualifications to work with F gas
facts: Guidance specifies personal qualifications for installation, service, leak checking, recovery and decommissioning activities.
Technician qualification is compliance evidence, not a greenhouse-gas measurement.

sources.title: How to operate or service electrical switchgear containing SF6
facts: SF6 switchgear guidance covers trained technicians and leak-check conditions, including specified exemptions.
Presence of SF6 or a leak-check threshold does not itself quantify SF6 emissions.

sources.title: Bans on F gas in new products and equipment current and future
facts: Guidance lists product and equipment restrictions by F-gas type, GWP and use.
A ban threshold or product restriction is regulatory scope rather than observed emissions.

sources.title: Banned F gas for refilling equipment
facts: Restrictions apply to specified high-GWP virgin F gases in large refrigeration systems with exceptions and reclaimed/recycled options.
Refill eligibility and refrigerant charge must not be equated with released mass.

sources.title: Selling F gas in cylinders or equipment
facts: Wholesalers and resellers must follow rules for F-gas cylinders and equipment already placed on the GB market.
Sale or market placement is supply-chain activity and does not prove physical emissions.

sources.title: Uses of F gas HFCs exempt from the phase down
facts: Some HFC uses are exempt from the phase-down and do not count towards quota, but must follow specified labelling or reporting rules.
Exempt status or reported exempt use does not establish emitted mass.

sources.title: Incumbent F gas quota holders and authorisation managers in Great Britain
facts: Official list identifies incumbent quota holders and authorisation managers for the 2024 to 2026 reference period.
Entity listing and quota entitlement are administrative provenance, not emissions observations.

sources.title: Import export or manufacture equipment pre-charged with F gas
facts: Pre-charged equipment importers may need registration, quota authorisations, declarations and reporting depending on CO2-equivalent quantities.
Pre-charged equipment quantity is contained product gas and must not be treated automatically as release.

sources.title: Environmental permitting landfill sector technical guidance
facts: Environment Agency collection links landfill gas management, monitoring, surface-emission, flare, engine and aftercare guidance.
Collection membership is provenance and regulatory scope, not a site emissions measurement.

sources.title: Management of landfill gas LFTGN 03
facts: LFTGN03 covers landfill gas impact assessment, control methods and monitoring within the regulatory framework.
Management requirements and risk assessment do not alone provide measured methane release.

sources.title: Monitoring trace components in landfill gas LFTGN 04
facts: LFTGN04 addresses concentration monitoring of priority trace components in raw landfill gas.
Gas concentration without supported flow and time does not establish mass emissions or parcel totals.

sources.title: Monitoring enclosed landfill gas flares LFTGN 05
facts: LFTGN05 provides methods for sampling, analysing and reporting emissions from enclosed landfill gas flares.
Flare monitoring must preserve measured species, flow, operating period and destruction context before mass-emission inference.

sources.title: Monitoring landfill gas surface emissions LFTGN 07
facts: LFTGN07 covers methane surface scanning, flux-box surveys, quantification, interpretation and reporting at permitted landfill sites.
A landfill surface-flux survey is site-specific evidence and is not automatically a cadastral parcel total.

sources.title: Monitoring landfill gas engine emissions LFTGN 08
facts: LFTGN08 covers emissions monitoring from spark-ignition landfill gas engines.
Engine-stack measurements and landfill surface methane are different emission pathways and must not be conflated.

sources.title: Landfill and deposit for recovery aftercare and permit surrender
facts: Aftercare guidance requires continued site management and monitoring, including landfill gas completion criteria, before permit surrender.
Permit surrender criteria and monitoring obligations are not themselves emissions observations.

sources.title: Landfill operators environmental permits manage landfill gas
facts: Operators must collect landfill gas and control subsurface migration and atmospheric surface emissions using site-specific systems and plans.
Gas collection or control requirements do not quantify uncaptured atmospheric release without measurement or supported calculation.

sources.title: Landfill methane measurement and metrics
facts: Environment Agency research assesses methods for measuring landfill methane emissions and potential regulatory use.
Research method performance and potential regulatory metrics must remain distinct from an actual measurement at a particular site.

sources.title: Regulating carbon capture utilisation and storage and offshore hydrogen production
facts: HSE explains duties under 2026 regulations extending offshore requirements to CCUS installations, CO2 pipelines and offshore hydrogen production from 6 April 2026.
Health and safety regulatory coverage does not establish captured, vented or stored CO2 quantities.

sources.title: Greenhouse gas removals independent review
facts: Independent review considers how GGR options including BECCS and DACCS can support UK net zero, with government response published 17 July 2026.
Policy review findings and technology potential are not observed removal quantities for a project or parcel.

sources.title: Decarbonisation readiness in environmental permit applications
facts: Environment Agency guidance applies to relevant new or substantially refurbished electricity-generating combustion plants for permit applications submitted on or after 28 February 2026.
Decarbonisation readiness is a permit-design requirement and is not evidence of current emissions reduction or carbon capture performance.

sources.title: CCS001 carbon capture and storage changes CO2 venting
facts: Ofgem approved CCS001 allowing specified CO2 venting between Delivery Point and Metering Point for network isolation, reconnection or maintenance contexts.
Permission for venting is not proof that venting occurred or a quantified CO2 release; event and measurement evidence is required.
